t: The Signature Vision: Soil Bot Networks
title: The Signature Vision: Soil Bot Networks
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Soil Bot Networks.
description:
The Signature vision of Soil Bot Networks does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature network hulls program, charter one: master burrowing bots at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale network logistics manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate soil sensing systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Soil Bot Networks becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

t: 2030 — First network hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses
title: 2030 — First network hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses
definition: 2030 milestone on the Soil Bot Networks roadmap.
description:
First network hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses, farms and root interaction construction sites.

What must be true first: the burrowing bots results have to replicate outside the lab, network logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and soil sensing operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed burrowing bots demonstrations, network logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting soil sensing uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Soil Bot Networks
definition: Estimates Soil Bot Networks readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Soil Bot Networks components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a network hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Soil Bot Networks Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Soil Bot Networks operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Soil Bot Networks installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 8603 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where burrowing bots monitoring, network logistics redundancy, or soil sensing maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Soil Bot Networks Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Soil Bot Networks: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Soil Bot Networks — underground robots tending soil health.

Phase 1 — Prove (burrowing bots): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (network logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (soil sensing): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (root interaction): network hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and agriculture-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
